review_text_raw:
My first experience with the found phone game genre was disappointing. I found [I]Replica[/I] to be an undercooked, preachy, borderline sciolistic game that is best not played. My excitement for this genre was quashed quickly, but I remembered that I still have [I]SIMULACRA[/I] in my backlog of games. Because of that, I decided to give found phone games another try.

Coincidentally, [I]SIMULACRA[/I] was partly inspired by [I]Replica[/I] (as seen by the titles), and partly by [I]Her Story[/I], one of my favourite games of all time. I loved [I]Her Story[/I] for its intriguing narrative and presentation, so I had some hope for [I]SIMULACRA[/I]. Thankfully, after my disheartening first exposure to found phone games, [I]SIMULACRA[/I] did not disappoint.

[I]SIMULACRA[/I] is a mystery game, in which you find a phone that belongs to a woman named Anna. By digging deep into her personal life chronicled by the contents of her phone and Internet activities, you uncover clues as to why Anna had gone missing. The puzzles in this game are fun, fair, and hardly difficult. Because of that, the game manages to present the story in a nice flow. It also helps that [I]SIMULACRA[/I] has a slick presentation, with a clean, Android-like user interface that controls well with mouse and keyboard. The in-game videos are pretty well done, too, but I did find the voice acting for one particular character to be laughable.

Despite [I]SIMULACRA[/I] being described or classified as a horror game, I did not find it scary.  Aside from a few instances, in which some players may find the game's version of a "jump scare" frightening, I considered this game to be more suspenseful. You can feel the plot thickening and tension building as the game progresses, with some subtle (but usually not so subtle) graphical and audio alterations making the game increasingly unnerving. The way [I]SIMULACRA[/I]'s story unfolds is almost Hitchcockian.

As much as I enjoyed the game narrative, I did find the ending slightly abrupt. It seemed like there is more story to tell, and perhaps the spin-off game, [I]SIMULACRA: Pipe Dreams[/I], may tie up some loose ends. Still, [I]SIMULACRA[/I] is a very enjoyable game, made even better if played in the dark with earphones on. The developers smartly included a "Begin+" mode that will unlock after the first playthrough. This mode allows you to replay the entire game with sped-up text, so you can retry certain scenarios without needing to sit through the slow, deliberate pace of the chat sessions. (It's also a time saver for achievement hunters.) [I]SIMULACRA[/I] gets an enthusiastic recommendation from me.

P.S.: I wrote this review after completing [I]Sara is Missing[/i] the predecessor of this game. [I]SIMULACRA[/I] shares many similarities with [I]S.I.M.[/I] (Coincidence? I think not!), and [I]SIMULACRA[/I] is clearly more refined in both story and game mechanics. Both games are worth playing, as they are both good ambassadors for the found phone game genre.

review_text_raw:
Simulacra is another game within the sara is missing universe. The first game was good but with new additions to a series brings new mechanics and fixes the short commings of the original, does this game do just that? I will be reviewing the game with a pro/ con style and end with my conclusion.

Pro:
     The game is very creepy. Now jumpscares are cheap and something I dont really enjoy but the game has ambient sound effects that are very spooky. Sometimes you may hear nocking at a door or a wisper or see the lights flicker in your field of view. Some are not really strong in spooking the player but the sound effects really sell the horror.

      The plot is good. Now this is pretty much a horror thriller game that delves with a deep mystery. The game throws you for many loops making you question who can you trust and how much information you should provide. You never know who is at the other end of that text message you recieved. The further you go the deeper the rabbit hole goes.

        The gameplay is simplistic. A game having a simplistic gameplay is nothing to fear. This is like playing a tale tell game where you get dialogue options but sometimes it effects the response of other players and the ending. There are branching paths but not many to get more than 2ish playthroughs. Still it is good to see that some choices creates a response that effect the story and feels a bit like a genuine response in a hypothetical world.

Con:
      There are some puzzles that are difficult. This game has quite a few moments that test memory and makes you search for clues to progress but some of these clues are very well hidden meaning in order to progress you might need to search the internet for the solution to save the frustration. It is a minor issue but i swear there is this one puzzle i could never solve.

Conclusion:
       In short this game is short but it is a blast to play. The story is creepy with atmoshere and has a great story. If you play the game for just a short ammount of time you will be hooked into finding out the truth. I can not reccomend this game enough for anything curious in the game. It is resonably priced in retrospect to how long the game is.

Decide for yourselves (moderate spoilers ahead):

2. Wanna get an okay-ish ending? [spoiler] - You have to trust a very, VERY untrustworthy registered sex offender and send him Anna's selfies and personal emails at his request and without Anna's consent. [/spoiler]

 [/spoiler]

review_text_raw:
A rather short game about a missing person.

You work on the missing persons mobile phone throughout the game and interact with Apps and send messages to persons.
While doing so, through music and ambient sounds, and a scare from time to time, this game creates an extremely intense atmosphere and pulls you into it's world!

Very, very good game. Highly recommend playing it. The 4€ are not much to pay for a couple hours of enjoyment!

I played it for a bit more than 5h now in one day.
In this time I completed my first and therefore truthful to my character playthrough, with a rather satisfying, though not "good" ending.
This took me around 4-4.5h

The remaining time, and time that will add from now on, is used for achivements, since this game let's you have them rather easily by reaching certain optional objectives that are never stated anywhere though ;)
So if you like to get into some secret hunting: This might be a game for you!

At the time of writing this review, I completed 4 out of 5 endings.
All of which are different enought to have their own twist to them! Really nice.

I know what the last ending will result in, but the details are yet unknown.

There are some negative points though, as no game is perfect.

Since we are talking about a "mobile game port" (to my knowledge that is), there are some essentials lacking.

This game features no settings menu of any kind.
It is not possible to lower the audio, except through the OS' sound mixer ...
That is not acceptable, far less in a post TB (TotalBiscuit) world.
Being able to lower Sound, Music and/or Video (which is sparsely used), would make this a more proper PC-game.
Also I haven't seen the possibility to change resolution, though the game is played only on about 10% of the screen anyway (due to the type of game it is ...)

There are subtitles hidden in the help-menu in main menu.

Especially in the later part of the game, the music is a tad too loud in comparison with the voices, so understanding suffers from it.

Other than the just stated? Not much to complain about.
Scrolling is a bit awkward, but works well enough by mousewheel and "dragging" via left click.
Typing in the places necessary is a bit lackluster since backspace deletes the whole last word (which can be a pain for fast typers that want to correct a misstype ...)

THats pretty much it.
Support this awsome dev!

review_text_raw:
A story about an idiot surrounded by other idiots who sound like idiots.

At no point was there any reason to sympathize with Anna and her lifetime of bad decisions that got her into this mess. She's like the stereotypical white person in a horror movie whose phone suddenly goes to static and runs out of gas in the middle of the night in front of an obviously haunted house and says "I should investigate this immediately, and by myself!". Her dumbass ex, her dumbass new lover, her dumbass "best friend", all of whom supposedly want to help her yet they somehow form the main obstacles to doing so, especially the "best friend" who is basically a secondary antagonist for all the help she is. Aside from bit players like the completely unconvincing cop. I thought the cop was lying about being a cop and that that was important as first, but nope, just terrible voice acting, we're supposed to believe that's what cops sound like. Though he's not as bad as the villain revealed at the end, who sounds like a 13 year old boy who got his big brother to install voice changing software for him because he thinks it'll make him sound badass on voice chat while playing Halo. It's that bad. Was it supposed to be intimidating? Was it supposed to be a shocking reveal? It wasn't, just the annoying end to a nonsensical story about thoroughly unsympathetic idiots. Nothing about this is redeemable, this was a waste of a Humble Bundle pick. And they had the nerve to release a sequel? Why, because they can churn out terrible games like this once a week? I hope it at least has an "everyone dies" ending, because after meeting all of these characters, I honestly don't want any of them to live, it would be better for society for every one of them to go away.

review_text_raw:
OK, I have just finished one run and I would recommend it!
In shorts,

Goods:
+Lots of contents, even some random guys on Spark, very detailed characterized even for minor characters
+Climax just bumped into at the right moments
+Innovative gameplay rather than just points and clicks
+Real action characters make the game much more immersive
+There are just right amount of minigames beside pure text reading
+Spot on the mentality that people like to check on others' phones and see what're inside, eg. Gallery, videos, etc
+Low price tag!

Bads:
-I can't say Anna is poor at acting, she's good, but she's kind of zoned out during the first second of most of the clips. It looks like that she is thinking what to say then starts acting after one second
-Some unnecessary jumpscares, the script is good, the story is good, come on, you can make the atmosphere scary without cheap jumpscares, make it more subtle, eg. Anna's wallpaper is changing after certain stages, which is spooky and good
-The ending is not so good... The whole process is great but when it comes to the ending... I am ok with the setting but it would be great if the ending part was made longer
-So during the ending part, Taylor is still busy texting you when he's encountering all those shxx? That doesn't make any sense. I understand that there has to be a means to let the players know what is happening. Can't you just make it like Taylor used Facetime with you before all those happened and try to tell the story with videos? As I imagine the scene, I found it very weird that Taylor is dealing with those things and keeps looking at the phone and texts you back and forth. That would be a heavy smartphone addict...
-The story is too long but very linear, which makes replays not quite possible. I want to try the other endings, but it's harsh for me to go for another 4-hour KNOWN adventure. There are many side events to do but the main route is pretty much the same. Maybe you can make it that we start at some certain late points or make the story less linear. We don't like grinding...

That being said, it's still a very great game, I hope there are more localization subtitles coming soon that I can refer to more of my friends from other parts of the world.
I will def buy the next title from Kaigon Games!
Good job! :p

review_text_raw:
It's good but you need to be able to look past 4 big faults to really get into it, as the game can kinda work on moon logic sometimes and it sets you up for failure, not to mention a few other plot holes. 

Also the story is completely railroaded, it has multiple endings but no matter which ending you're going to get, the story and game is pretty much the exact same aside from VERY MINOR character dialog and Ashley not talking to you depending on your choices, until the final scene where it will use choices you made in the past and whether or not you do a specific thing right before the final scene, to determine if Anna and Taylor, the two main characters, are destined to die, or if not, whether or not only one of them will live or if both of them are going to live.

It only branches out and stops being railroaded in the climax and resolution of the game, and since it outright encourages you to replay it to get all the endings, it can't really get away with assuming that people will only play it once, especially since it's extremely easy to fall into the worst ending if you don't do everything right.

Outside of these things, and if you can get past it, this game is good and fun, an intriguing concept and I like Taylor even if he's a total dork. But don't play the phone version as the loops in audio are not as smooth as on the PC version and I experienced a bug that ruined every FMV in the final scene, so you should get it on steam for PC like here.

This game isn't a very good game.

The story is kinda boring since all you do for the majority the game is follow directions from two incredibly annoying characters. 
You get very little freedome in the game and rarely get to "solve" anything. There are only two types of puzzels and the mechanics are so shallow that I hesitate to even call them puzzels. 
There are video's that get unlocked while you progress through the game. And for the most part they are useless.
The acting is god awfle for the most part and the dialogue is terrible. 

To call this a horror game would be an insult to horror games. And most horror games aren't good so that says a lot. the jumpscares are very bad. For the most part they are just randome noises or images that are just there to give you a jump. and it's fucking obnoxious. I don't know what this game wants to be because it fails on every single aspect.

One thing that I actually like about this game has nothing to do with the story. and that is the screen on the sides that isn't the phone screens. The sounds that were made "IRL" were a nice touch to pull you into the game and make you feel uneasy. I liked it untill I looked up this game and learnt that this was a phone game. Which meant that It was impossible for the game to do something creative with the side screens like actually making you walk around the house or for someome to meet you "IRL".

the first thirty minutes were pretty good because it hadn't shown how awfle the writing and acting was. it was all down hill from there...

And the ending is fucking stupid. It's so fucking bad.
